Design rationaleUI ARCHITECT

Zone 1 · Identity

Single row · ticker + sector + price + verdict chip. No redundancy.

Verdict chip is 3 segments (call / tier / score) but reads as ONE unit. Eye locks on it in < 200ms.

Background gradient hints at verdict color without shouting.

Zone 2 · Action context

4 KPI tiles answer: what · how risky · key levels · how much.

Sub-line per tile carries the modifier ("ENTRY extended", "catalyst window") — context without separate banner.

Mode pills + lead-lens live below the tiles as secondary chrome, not their own bar.

Zone 3 · Multi-lens bar

8 lenses as color-coded micro-pills · scannable in 1 glance.

Direction arrow + 1 metric per lens · no verbose "1-5Y MoS −26%" strings.

Conflict badge at right shows count · expand reveals full prose only when needed.

Information-hierarchy principles applied:
  1. One verdict, one location — current design shows BUY in 3 places · this shows it once with maximum prominence.
  2. Typography > space — primary 28px, secondary 16px, tertiary 10.5px. Eye orders attention by size, not by row.
  3. Tiles beat text strings — "STOP $241 · T1 $260 · T2 $278" reads faster than the same data in a prose row.
  4. Progressive disclosure — conflict text is a badge that expands. Most users glance · power users drill.
  5. Color = meaning, not decoration — green = bull, red = bear, amber = caution, copper = primary accent. Used sparingly.
